clue.text: Insubstantial state, not watertight

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
something porous lets water through, so it is not watertight

explanation.surface: A description of a leaky, flimsy government or condition that cannot hold water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like part of the definition but supplies VA, Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour has no solid body, so something like vapour is flimsy and lacking substance.

clue.text: Exposed, ring up lawyers, having reached end of line

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for ring is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them
the Bar is the collective name for barristers

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: Someone phones a firm of lawyers and finds their secrets exposed when the call reaches the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIAL into LAID; 'end of' takes E from line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exposed has been uncovered and stripped of its covering, an idiom for revealed.

clue.text: English writer's drink

definitions.meaning: Robert ... was an English poet and novelist, author of I, Claudius
a wine from the Bordeaux region of France named after its gravelly soil

explanation.surface: A question of what a particular English author liked to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: Robert Graves the poet and novelist, and the Bordeaux wine district's red or white wine.

clue.text: Major character of Shaw, one introduced by two snatches of music

indicators.note: introduced by puts the musical pieces in front of the letter for one
two asks for the word for a snatch of music to be written twice

parts.note: a bar is a short measure of music
A as the indefinite article means one

explanation.surface: A theatrical character brought onstage with a couple of bursts of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' reads as an adjective but is part of the play's title, Major Barbara by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play Major Barbara is named after its heroine, a Salvation Army officer.

clue.text: Coptic bishop books into mutual help organisation

indicators.note: into places the letters for books inside the organisation's letters

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a self-help fellowship
B is an abbreviation for book, so books gives two of them

explanation.surface: A churchman's books are placed with a support group.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Coptic and Syriac churches the title Father, from Aramaic, is given to bishops and patriarchs.

clue.text: Goliath, ear-bending a saint worshipper

indicators.note: bending twists the letters of the giant's name and ear into a new order

explanation.surface: The giant Goliath lectures someone devoted to saints at tedious length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ear-bending' is an idiom for talking at someone; here 'ear' is fodder and 'bending' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hagiolatry is the veneration of saints, and one who practises it is so named.

clue.text: Risk a section of the church abandoning Latin

indicators.note: abandoning tells us to drop the letter for Latin from the church part

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar

explanation.surface: A priest considers the danger of a church area losing its Latin services.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a gamble is to risk something; as a verb, the two are synonyms.

clue.text: City in Arabic translated as "Italian boot"

indicators.note: in places the city's letters inside the rearranged word
translated changes the form of Arabic, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city's name rendered from Arabic into a phrase about Italian footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like the definition, but it supplies LA; the quoted 'Italian boot' is the region's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: This region forms the toe and lower foot of the boot-shaped Italian peninsula.

clue.text: Drug-taking composer greeting American-style rock group drained of energy, forming another band

indicators.note: taking means the composer's name takes in the drug letter

parts.note: J S Bach, the German composer
E is short for the drug ecstasy
bo is a US form of address to a pal, as in 'hey, bo'

indicators.note: drained of means the energy letter is removed

parts.note: Yes is a British progressive rock band
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rock music tale of a composer on drugs greeting an exhausted band before forming a new group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained of energy' takes E from YES to leave YS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian surf-pop group behind Good Vibrations is a band distinct from Yes.

clue.text: Kind doctor Rex with line in old-fashioned salutation

parts.note: a kind person is good
MO is a medical officer
R stands for Rex, king, as in royal signatures
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A kindly doctor named Rex greets someone with an old-fashioned line.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic greeting meaning a pleasant day to you, used in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Shakes off visitor ban

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone throws off a ban imposed on a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakes off' reads as one verb, but 'Shakes' is the definition and 'off' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremors and quivers are plural nouns for shaking movements; synonyms.

clue.text: "Straits" can be heard

definitions.meaning: narrow sea channels, like Plymouth or Puget's
makes a noise, as a bell or alarm does

explanation.surface: A remark that a word for sea passages is audible.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow sea channels share their name with the verb for making a noise.

clue.text: Axon displays cool courage taking roughage

parts.note: nerve is calm bravery
fibre is roughage in the diet

explanation.surface: Someone shows bravery by eating their bran.
explanation.definitionFit: An axon is the long thread-like part of a neuron that carries impulses, a biology term.

clue.text: Bean collected by Rose and checked

indicators.note: collected by places the bean inside the colour word

parts.note: rose is a pinkish red colour
a pulse is an edible seed such as a bean

explanation.surface: A gardener named Rose gathers a bean crop and inspects it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name but is the colour, RED.
explanation.definitionFit: An attack that is checked has been driven back or repelled.

clue.text: Fit revolving stage after lead's made an exit

indicators.note: revolving turns the shortened word round to read the other way
the lead is the first letter, and it has left the word

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A theatre scene: a revolving stage fitted after the leading actor exits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is a fit of pique; STEP loses its lead S to give TEP, which revolving turns to PET.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pet is to sulk in a huff, a temper tantrum.

clue.text: Round variety of raisin associated with a deity

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: a variety of the dried fruit means its letters in another order

explanation.surface: A certain type of dried grape is linked to a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Osiris, the Egyptian god of the underworld; adjective from the deity's name.

clue.text: Old foreign coin without a name

indicators.note: without tells us to take away the a from the coin

parts.note: the anna was an old Indian coin, a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.surface: An old foreign coin turns up with no name on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A female forename, here an example of a name.

clue.text: Seaside plant's unvarying energy

parts.note: static means unchanging
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A coastal plant has steady vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lavender, a coastal flowering plant, is known by this genus name.

clue.text: Tipless battleaxe is my creative way of unfairly favouring allies

indicators.note: tipless means the battleaxe word loses its end letter

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman, like a battleaxe

indicators.note: creative means the two small words are arranged inventively

explanation.surface: A formidable old woman explains her own style of corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouritism shown to friends, especially in appointments to political office.

clue.text: Rock group's No 1 passed onto Italian earl

indicators.note: No 1 means the first letter of the word group

parts.note: time ran, meaning passed
IT is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A band's number one hit is handed to an Italian aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock group' reads as a band, but 'Rock' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard igneous stone used for building and worktops.

clue.text: Velocity regulator using gravitational force in preference to negative resistance

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational acceleration
choosing one thing over another means in preference to it
no is a negative answer
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A physics puzzle about a speed device using gravity rather than resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical device that automatically controls the speed of an engine.

clue.text: Zip attached to cooker shade

parts.note: zip is nothing, which is O
a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: A zip fastening is attached to a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour, shade meaning a hue.

clue.text: See 10
End up restricting Sam's development, creating a bad atmosphere

indicators.note: restricting means the reworked name is held inside
in a down clue, up reads the word for end from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim

indicators.note: development means the letters of Sam are worked into a new order

parts.note: the name Sam

explanation.surface: Sam's growth is held back in a gloomy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' means an aim or goal here, not a finish; 'up' and 'development' both act on it and on Sam.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious vapour or an oppressive feeling, a bad air.

clue.text: Crude African oil which has a major fault

indicators.note: crude means rough, unrefined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A report on African crude oil with a serious flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude oil' reads as one phrase, but 'Crude' is the signal and 'oil' fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state is crossed by the San Andreas Fault, a major geological fault line.

clue.text: City's abbreviated text breaking agreement

indicators.note: breaking means the text letters split the agreement word

parts.note: OK expresses agreement
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A city's short message breaks a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Siberian city in Russia on the Irtysh river.

clue.text: See 9
See 2
Tom 26, possibly, wants retro outfit with hollowed lapels

indicators.note: retro means backward, so the outfit word reads in reverse

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing

indicators.note: hollowed empties the word lapels, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone wants a retro outfit with the lapels cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is BOYS; tomboys may be female, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomboys are, in all likelihood, female children, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: It's a mark around small tree

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A mark is drawn round a little tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub or small tree with feathery foliage that grows in salty coastal soils.
